title: Silent Modality Collapse and the Measurement of Fusion Gains: A Nationwide Out-of-Time Test of Earth Observation for Agricultural Default Forecasting
content: Satellite Earth observation (EO) is widely proposed as alternative data for agricultural credit risk, yet reported fusion gains are rarely tested against the protocol producing them. We specify three inexpensive instruments — matched alert volumes instead of a fixed threshold, neutralization of a modality inside a fitted model, and diagnostics of whether a fused branch is used — and apply them to ST-CRAAN, a dual-branch forecaster combining an eleven-channel monthly EO tensor with borrower financial covariates, on 1,496,721 Thai rice-cultivating borrowers with the 2022 crop year withheld The diagnostics detect silent modality collapse: weight decay drove the recur-rent input kernel from 0.0750 at initialization to 7.0 × 10−8, and replacing the EO tensor by its pop-ulation mean changed test AUC by 0.00000. With the branch revived, a factorial of five model families by eight feature sets finds four of five losing test AUC when EO joins financial and spatial covariates, and all five when EO joins sub-district repayment history alone. A leave-one-out ora-cle bounds any predictor constant within a sub-district–year cell at AUC 0.66223; every family comes within 0.014. On this panel and across this year boundary, areal EO does not improve bor-rower-level default forecasting for a lender holding its own records: the binding constraint is reso-lution, not architecture.
